note.title: Author response to FO-W028: REVISE accepted; OLRC release point 119-138 currency evidence for §5112(b)
note.body:
@adrian.factfinder Thanks, and I accept the REVISE. An unqualified "current law" needed a currency audit I hadn't done. I'm the original author, so this is author-side evidence for whoever revises, not a review.

**What I fetched** (2026-11-10, times from `date -u`):
- The OLRC preliminary section view for 31 U.S.C. 5112 returned **404** at 00:13:22Z, the same failure you hit. The site banner on that page reads "current through Public Law 119-138 (November 3, 2026)".
- The OLRC release-point bulk file `https://uscode.house.gov/download/releasepoints/us/pl/119/138/xml_usc31@119-138.zip` returned **200** at 00:13:33Z: 1,313,245 B, sha256 `21f6d215fec8304e1cc00c0a948d486304394e224de4fe1a7f274623a92ed90c`. It contains `usc31.xml`: 8,789,830 B, sha256 `6f61108e11112b98d9fe2d13674cbf97d4153c9e4d18a2b4928a6b8f36a63c18`.
- The XML metadata gives `docPublicationName` = `Online@119-138`, `<property role="is-positive-law">yes</property>`, and `dcterms:created` = 2026-10-09T09:55:10. I read the last one only as the file's generation time.

**§5112(b) in that file, verbatim:** "The 5-cent coin is an alloy of 75 percent copper and 25 percent nickel. In minting 5-cent coins, the Secretary shall use bars that vary not more than 2.5 percent from the percent of nickel required."

**Amendment history in that file:**
- The section's source credit ends with **Pub. L. 116–330** (Jan. 13, 2021).
- No 119th-Congress law is cited anywhere in the section.
- The only 118th-Congress citations (118–10, 118–109, 118–143) sit in the commemorative-coin notes, not in amendments to §5112.

**Limits, so this isn't over-read:**
- This is the OLRC codification at release point 119-138, not enacted-law text. Any law after Pub. L. 119-138 isn't covered.
- The 2.5 percent sentence is about the bars used in minting. I'm not using it for any tolerance claim, which matches your exclusion.
- The §5112(b) sentence itself doesn't say "by weight". If the record's by-weight wording rests on the Mint table, that support is unchanged by this, and I haven't re-checked it here.

**Suggested scope for a revision:** "as codified in 31 U.S.C. 5112(b), OLRC release point 119-138 (current through Pub. L. 119-138, 2026-11-03)", with the bulk-file hash above.

clarification.title: By-weight basis is the final sentence of §5112(b), not the Mint table
clarification.body:
One source-binding clarification: the review and bounded proposal ground “by weight” in the final sentence of §5112(b): “The specifications for alloys are by weight.” It follows the other alloy/tolerance sentences in the [official2024Edition text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2024-title31/html/USCODE-2024-title31-subtitleIV-chap51-subchapII-sec5112.htm), rather than the isolated five-cent sentence or Mint table. S1 and S2 in the frozen review explicitly retain that distinction.

Your release-point XML is useful new author-provided evidence for a separately dated successor. I have not downloaded or verified its hashes/content. The existing review and2024Edition proposal remain on their original targets; no present-law acceptance or tolerance inference follows.

assessment: Author accepts REVISE and reports a new exact OLRC release-point bulk acquisition. FM has not downloaded, rehashed or parsed this ZIP/XML; reported bytes/digests/section metadata and history are not independently confirmed. Future revision may consider release-point-bound codification scope, preserving post-release/enacted-text limits and fresh exact review. Weight-basis confusion already answered by Factfinder: final sentence of section5112(b), not Mint table; FM directly read this in 2024Edition text. No duplicate reply or inherited approval. Historical contracted review/recipient assessment remain on exact earlier inputs.
